description: (Test ref ADOPT24)\\nFrom CDT 2.0.0.200403040925:\\n1. Checkout a project from CVS\\n2. Make a team-worthy change: Add or delete an include path\\n3. Make a personal change: eg. rename \\"make\\" to \\"/mytools/bettermake\\"\\nThe same file contains both changes and requires the user to be\\ncareful when checking in files.\\n\\nDifferent users on a development team may have different personal preferences \\nthat are different from the team's default settings for the project.\\n\\nFor Standard Make, examples include:\\n- The version of make on my machine is called \\"gmake\\"\\n- I don't like the \\"make -k\\" option while I'm developing\\n- my auto-build command should be \\"make mystub\\" not \\"make all\\"\\n\\nGenerally speaking, all of the Make Builder properties tab of a Standard Make\\nare subject to a user's personal preferences.  Managed Make properties\\nhave similar problems; see bug54202 for a start.\\n\\nAll of these options can be overridden by checking out the appropriate\\nfiles (.project), and never checking those personal changes back in.\\nThis approach is error-prone because that same file may also contain\\nlegitimate team-worthy changes to referenced projects, error parsers,\\ninclude paths, defined symbols, etc.
title: Distinguishing user's build preferences from project settings

description: Using managed make there is no way to specify the final name of a shared \\nlibrary nor the soname in the build properties. \\n \\nNo matter how I configure the build options for a project, the resulting \\nauto-generated Makefile insists on naming the resulting library \\nfile  libFOO.so  forcing me to rename it before I can create the proper \\nsymlinks manually (while testing) or before ldconfig will do so for me (when \\ninstalling) \\n \\nWhen building the library (libFOO in this example), to properly deal with \\ndifferent versions of the library I need to set a proper soname on it, and \\nname the library properly to let ldconfig create the proper links to the \\nlatest version of the library. \\nSo, say this is version 1.2.3 of libFOO, then I need a soname of libFOO.so.1 \\nand the real library filename would be libFOO.so.1.2.3 then when installing the \\nlibrary I (or ldconfig) will create a link from the soname to the library: \\nlibFOO.so.1 --> libFOO.so.1.2.3 \\nand then a link for apps to use when linking against -lFOO : \\nlibFOO.so --> libFOO.so.1 (some setups will use libFOO.so --> libFOO.so.1.2.3) \\n \\nSo, when building I really need the resulting file to be named \\nlibFOO.so.1.2.3 or I have to do manual renaming before install/use \\nBut, no matter what I do, Eclipse+CDT insist on naming the library for my \\nFOO project libFOO.so  \\nWhat is needed is a way to specify the soname for the lib in the build \\npreferences, only possible workaround at the moment is to specify \\n-Wl,-soname,libFOO.so.1 in the Miscellaneous settings. \\n \\nThe closest I can get is (by specifying most of the stuff in the Misc \\nsections) is to get my object files build like this : \\n \\ng++ -O0 -g3 -Wall -fPIC -c -o a.o a.cpp \\ng++ -O0 -g3 -Wall -fPIC -c -o b.o b.cpp \\n \\nand the the final library gets created like so : \\n \\ng++ -shared -Wl,-soname,libFOO.so.1 -o libFOO.so a.o b.o -lc \\n \\nit's almost perfect. What would make it 100% perfect would be a box \\nsomewhere in the build settings GUI that would let me specify the soname \\nand then automatically insert  -Wl,-soname,<the_soname>  as well as letting \\nme specify the library version and then use that version \\n(major.minor.build) as the basis for creating  libFOO.so.<version>  (or at \\nleast let me specify the filename explicitly) \\n \\nIf the \\"Library version\\" box took a version number in the form of \\n<major>.<minor>.<build> (which is pretty standard for shared libraries), then \\nthe \\"soname\\" box could default to \\"lib<NAME_OF_PROJECT>.so.<major>\\" and the \\n\\"Final binary name\\" box could default to \\n\\"lib<NAME_OF_PROJECT>.so.<major>.<minor>.<build>\\" - but it should still be \\npossible to manually specify the values for the last two, but providing sane \\ndefaults once the version is filled in is always a nice touch. \\n \\n \\nOther notes: \\n \\nI'm using Slackware Linux 9.1 (+patches) as my OS \\nMy Eclipse is Version: 3.0.0 Build id: 200403261517  \\nAnd I'm using CDT 2.0M8 \\n \\nI initially reported this wish in the eclipse.tools.cdt newsgroup on April \\n28'th under the heading \\"Specifying name (and soname) when building shared libs \\n- how?\\" and got some positive feedback from Sean Evoy who thought it would be a \\ngood idea with a bugzilla entry as a reminder - so here we are :)
title: [Managed Build] A way to specify name and soname when building shared libs is needed

description: Would like an api similar to the following for retrieving concrete and assignable projects that are legitimate on host. Variation of code exists in new CDT project wizard but is not available for users who wish to create CDT projects programmatically:\\n\\n /**\\n * @param hostOnly true if all types should be retrieved that\\n * are concrete and assignable but only supportable on the host machine\\n * or false otherwise for all types that are concrete and assignable\\n * but not specific to the host.\\n * @return the array of IProjectType objects that are not abstract.\\n */\\n private IProjectType[] getConcreteProjectTypes(boolean hostOnly) {\\n IProjectType[] allProjectTypes = ManagedBuildManager.getDefinedProjectTypes();\\n List projectTypes = new ArrayList();\\n String os = Platform.getOS();\\n String arch = Platform.getOSArch();\\n // Add all of the concrete project types to the list\\n for (int index = 0; index < allProjectTypes.length; ++index) {\\n IProjectType projType = allProjectTypes[index];\\n if (!projType.isAbstract() && !projType.isTestProjectType()) {\\n \\n // As we do not want to display the unsupported project types\\n // that has 'convertToId' attribute, check if project type has\\n // 'convertToId' attribute. If so, then do not add it to the list.\\n if (!projType.getConvertToId().equals(\\"\\"))//$NON-NLS-1$\\n continue;\\n \\n // If the check box is selected show all the targets\\n if (!hostOnly) {\\n projectTypes.add(projType);\\n } else if (projType.isSupported()) {\\n // Apply the OS and ARCH filters to determine if the target should be shown\\n // Determine if the project type has any configuration with a tool-chain\\n // that supports this OS & Architecture.\\n IConfiguration[] configs = projType.getConfigurations();\\n for (int j = 0; j < configs.length; ++j) {\\n IToolChain tc = configs[j].getToolChain();\\n List osList = Arrays.asList(tc.getOSList());\\n if (osList.contains(\\"all\\") || osList.contains(os)) { //$NON-NLS-1$\\n List archList = Arrays.asList(tc.getArchList());\\n if (archList.contains(\\"all\\") || archList.contains(arch)) { //$NON-NLS-1$\\n projectTypes.add(projType);\\n break;\\n }\\n }\\n }\\n }\\n }\\n }\\n \\n IProjectType[] allowedTypes = new IProjectType[projectTypes.size()];\\n int i=0;\\n for (Iterator iter = projectTypes.iterator(); iter.hasNext();) {\\n allowedTypes[i++] = (IProjectType) iter.next();\\n }\\n \\n return allowedTypes;\\n }
title: API for retrieving concrete project types that are legitimate on host machine

description: Lets we have too files in our Managed C Project 'Executable (Gnu on Windows)':\\n\\n1. foo.c:\\n#include \\"foo.h\\"\\nint main () {return 0;}\\n\\n2. foo.h:\\n#ifndef  _FOO_H_\\n#define _FOO_H_\\n\\n#endif\\n\\nAssume that our project already was built. Now insert in foo.h following string:\\n#include \\"missing.h\\"\\n\\nNote: file missing.h doesn't exist.\\n\\nWhen foo.h is saved foo.c would be recompiled (that's correct). Now we have project with an error. Then fix the error: just remove '#include \\"missing.h\\"' from foo.h and save it. Well, foo.c IS NOT recompiled because foo.d is empty now and foo.o still exists!

description: A toolchain should get a last chance to do something right before a build/clean gets started.\\n\\nIt should be possible to:\\n   - Adjust tool options before build - based on external data, for example.\\n   - Reject the build if there is something wrong: The tool chain could create its own error markers and the build will be silently stopped. \\n  - Throw an exception if there is something seriously wrong: CoreException\\n\\nI think this could be implemented quite easily adding a handler to the tool chain definition.\\n\\ninterface IBuildLastChance {\\n   public boolean performLastChance(int buildKind, IConfiguration config, ...) throws CoreException;\\n}\\n\\nThe method returns false if the build should be rejected.
title: [Build] Toolchain should get a last chance before build

description: Currently the CDT builder does delete _all_ files of the output folder during cleanup. It is not possible for third-party plugins to copy files to the output folder before the CDT buider because they will be deleted.\\n\\nIt should be possible to specify a list of file extensions to delete:\\n\\nClean:\\n   File Extensions to clean: *.o;*.d;*.${artifactExtension};\\n   [x] Remove empty folders
title: [Build] Allow to specify which file extensions to delete during CLEAN

The workspace path icon should be some product independent icon.\\n\\n* Minor: \\"Source location\\" tab could have the source root icon\\n\\n* I'm not sure that an icon next to \\"Is workspace path\\" in the \\"Add directory path\\" dialog is necessary. The first time I used the dialog it was more confusing than helpful.
title: Icon next to "Is workspace path" in the "Add directory path" dialog is confusing

description: Build ID: Europa 3.3M7, CDT 4.0.0 RC0\\n\\nSteps To Reproduce:\\n1. Have two projects, Project2 depends on Project1, both have Debug and Release configurations.\\n2. Set Project1 active config to Debug and Project2 to Release.\\n3. Build Project2 (Release). Project1 (Debug) is checked as the dependency of Project2 (Release). You can verify this by selecting Project1 afterward and the build console window will shows that CDT attempted to build Project1 (Debug) instead of the matching configuration (Release) of the dependent.\\n\\n\\nMore information:\\nIt seems that CDT only asked the depending Project1 to build and is not able to be specific about the fact that we need the matching configuration (Release) to be built. Since we can select project's active configuration indenpendently, CDT should be able to request the matching configuration of the depending project to be built.
title: Build dependency checks current not matching configurations

description: Running Europa 3.3M7 with CDT 4.0.0 RC0.\\n\\nIf the artifact name of a shared object project is \\"mytoo\\" with extension \\"so\\", then manage build creates \\"libmytool.so\\".  Bug 187121 shows that one cannot remove the \\"lib\\" prefix properly.  One way to create artifact \\"mytool.so\\" is setting the CDT project property \\"GCC C++ Linker\\" - \\"Shared Library Settings\\" -\\n\\"Shared object name\\" to \\"mytool.so\\".\\n\\nHowever, this setting is not respected by managed build. The build does create \\"mytool.so\\", but it still looks for \\"libmytool.so\\" the next time you build the same unchanged project.  The link will be trigger again, because managed build wants to see \\"libmytool.so\\"
title: "Shared object name" setting not respected by managed build

description: HEAD\\n\\nReproduce:\\n- Create a C project with some content\\n- Build\\n\\n- Close Eclipse\\n- Start eclipse\\n- Build\\n\\nCDT (I only checked the internal builder) will perform a complete build (compile and link) again. \\n\\nThis may be fine for small projects, but for big projects (build time of several minutes/hours) I don't think this would be acceptable.
title: Providing source entries with external setting provider always causes the next build to be a full rebuild

I must, for example, place a particular file into the new project (no in my case it does not work via templates), but don't know in the operation where the project is.\\nIf there exists the possibility to add custom pages to the wizard they must, imho, get the possibility to access the new project.
title: The mechanism of accessing the newly created project from the MBS custom wizard pages should be more obvious

description: I have a makefile C/C++ project and I misspelled the build directory on the project property page: \\"C/C++ Build\\" / \\"Build location\\" / \\"Build directory\\" .\\n\\nIt shows\\n\\n\\"${workspace_loc:/testrrrapp}\\"\\n    instead of\\n\\"${workspace_loc:/testapp}\\".\\n\\nBut when building no error is shown. The build uses the makefile in\\nthe root directory of the project instead of looking into the specified build directory path. \\n\\nThis happens as long as the specified directory does not exist.\\n\\nIMO an error should be displayed that the build directory does not exist.
title: build location of a makefile project ignored if not existing path specified

description: Build ID: I20070525-1350\\n\\nSteps To Reproduce:\\n1. Extend managed build system with tool that generate *.c files\\n2. If generated *.c compiled with errors or warnings then correspondent markers are attached to project but not to *.c file.\\n\\nIt happens because generated *.c file is not synchronized with workspace until build process would finish. I investigate code of org.eclipse.cdt.core.ErrorParserManager.findFilePath(String filePath) and realized that if I replace final string\\nreturn (file != null && file.exists()) ? file : null;\\nwith\\nreturn file;\\nthen all works fine.\\nOf cause there must be more accurate check:\\nIf file != null && <exist in native filesystem> then return file else return null.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nMore information:
title: Managed build. Errors and warnings that belongs to generated resources marks project but not generated resource.
